eligibility: A 2026 theatrical release by the cutoff.
An explicitly quantified loss forecast in dated original film-industry trade reporting, attributed to industry or financial sources.
A budget/gross gap, generic calculator, reader prediction or unattributed model is not eligible.
ranking: Descending upper estimate; equal upper estimates share a rank. Ties are displayed by descending lower estimate, then title.
limits: This is a ranking of the largest comparable published forecasts located in a documented review, not a census of all films or verified actual losses.
Dates and accounting assumptions differ, and full financial models are not public.
Original forecasts are preserved, not recalculated using later ticket sales.
Missing forecasts remain unknown, not zero or necessarily smaller than the fourth film.
The full 2026 release schedule was consulted, but its thousand-plus titles were not individually financially audited.

discovery.filter: Reported budget at least $25M, worldwide gross below 2.5 times that budget, and a 2026 US release. This prioritizes research only, not a break-even rule or proof of loss.

candidates.title: Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu

discovery.searchCoverage: Broad 2026 film bomb/loss searches and title searches using loss, lose, forecast, Deadline, Variety, TheWrap and Hollywood Reporter. The largest omitted-film claims were traced to original reporting or their actual stated calculation.

qualifyingReports.title: Digger
qualifyingReports.basis: Includes post-theatrical revenue; different insiders give different estimates.
qualifyingReports.assumption: The report expected worldwide box office not to exceed $40 million. Its other source made the loss dependent on premium video-on-demand performance.

qualifyingReports.title: Moana
qualifyingReports.basis: First-cycle loss forecast, including revenue after cinemas.
qualifyingReports.assumption: The forecast assumed a final worldwide box office of $250 million.

qualifyingReports.title: Supergirl
qualifyingReports.basis: First-cycle loss forecast, including downstream income after cinemas.
qualifyingReports.assumption: Published after a $68 million worldwide opening. The report gives a $315 million worldwide break-even estimate, but does not specify the final worldwide gross assumed in its $125 million loss forecast.

qualifyingReports.title: The Bride!
qualifyingReports.basis: Loss could approach $90 million in the first cycle, after home entertainment revenue.
qualifyingReports.assumption: Published after a $13.6 million worldwide opening. No final worldwide gross assumption is specified in the report.

reviewedAlternatives.finding: The reported $150M budget and tiny ticket sales establish underperformance, not net loss. ReelTally subtracts global gross from budget, omitting exhibitor shares, marketing and later income. Its roughly $149M gap is not eligible.

reviewedAlternatives.status: Located $140M to $150M claim uses a different method
reviewedAlternatives.finding: FilmDB derives its estimate from a $170M to $200M production budget and about half of $115M box office. It does not supply a sourced first-cycle model including later income. The trade reports reviewed confirm underperformance, but do not quantify a comparable net-loss forecast.

Variety quotes $80M to $85M and $100M to $120M theatrical losses under roughly $200M global-gross assumptions. Use Deadline's explicitly first-cycle $125M forecast without importing Variety's assumptions.

Variety reports $100M for The Bride! theatrically, $80M for Supergirl, $25M to $40M for The End of Oak Street, and $30M to $40M for Practical Magic 2 theatrically. A source disputes the last estimate and expects a $5M profit. These are not mixed into first-cycle forecasts.
Variety describes theatrical losses as tens of millions. That is neither a precise numeric interval nor a first-cycle forecast.

The original reports reviewed discuss underperformance without a comparable quantified first-cycle loss. The $100M theatrical-loss sentence in the Disney CEO article refers to Moana, not this film. Fan-model $150M claims are excluded.
The $103M theatrical shortfall uses assumed marketing and a generic 50% ticket-rental rule. It is not original reporting of a first-cycle loss forecast.
The original report gives a $30M production budget and weak opening, not a quantified first-cycle loss. Secondary guesses with assumed marketing are excluded.

reviewedAlternatives.status: Rights sale and write-down are different measures
reviewedAlternatives.finding: A contemplated tax write-down and rights sale are not a first-cycle loss forecast for the 2026 release. No qualifying forecast was verified.

corrections: Supergirl changes from Variety's $80M to $120M theatrical-only estimates to Deadline's $125M first-cycle forecast.
Supergirl and Moana share second place by upper estimate.
